title: Tangent cone and minimal-prime dimensions of an essentially smooth local extension
statement:
Let $(A,\mathfrak m,K)$ and $(B,\mathfrak n,L)$ be nonzero local commutative $\mathbf Q$-algebras essentially of finite type (localizations of finitely generated $\mathbf Q$-algebras) [def-weil-pbc-essentially-finite-type-algebra]. Let $A\to B$ be a local homomorphism which is essentially smooth [def-weil-pbc-essentially-smooth-ring-map], meaning a localization of a smooth algebra. Set $F=B/\mathfrak mB$ and $s=\dim F$ [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring]. Then $F$ is regular local [def-weil-regular-scheme], and there is an isomorphism of graded $L$-algebras
$$\operatorname{gr}_{\mathfrak n}B\simeq (L\otimes_K\operatorname{gr}_{\mathfrak m}A)[T_1,\ldots,T_s],$$
where associated graded rings are $\bigoplus_{j\ge0}\mathfrak m^j/\mathfrak m^{j+1}$ and similarly for $B$ [def-weil-pbc-associated-graded-ring], $T_i$ have degree one, and the isomorphism restricts to the induced map on the base graded algebra. Moreover the sets of dimensions of minimal-prime quotients satisfy
$$\{\dim(B/\mathfrak q):\mathfrak q\text{ a minimal prime of }B\}=\{\dim(A/\mathfrak p)+s:\mathfrak p\text{ a minimal prime of }A\}.$$
No bijection of minimal primes, and no equality of residue fields, is asserted.

source.place: Tags 00T7 (lemma-standard-smooth) and 00ON (lemma-dimension-base-fibre-equals-total), local smooth-chart and dimension inputs; the graded comparison is a further local-algebra lemma, not the statement of either tag. Detailed smooth Hilbert--Samuel input WANTED: BMT arXiv:0905.3580, section 6.3, cited by ILO VIII 2.3.13.

proof.text: Write $B=P_{\mathfrak N}$ for a smooth finite type $A$-algebra $P$ and a prime $\mathfrak N$ over $\mathfrak m$, using the localization description of an essentially smooth local algebra. Both $A$ and $B$ are Noetherian: take their finite type $\mathbf Q$-algebra models and apply the finite type Noetherian theorem followed by localization. Smoothness gives $A\to P$ flat; localization and transitivity give $A\to B$ flat. The smooth-fibre theorem identifies $F=B/\mathfrak mB$ with a localization of the smooth $K$-algebra $P\otimes_AK$ and proves it regular local. In particular its dimension $s$ is finite.

source.place: Tags 00FN (Noetherian permanence), 00TA (smooth flatness), 00T4 and 00TT (smooth fibres), 00P1 (finite local dimension).

proof.text: Apply the relative Cohen presentation to the flat local map just obtained. Choose the compatible coefficient sections, put $R=K[[X_1,\ldots,X_e]]$, and write $\widehat A=R/I$ and $\widehat B=L[[X_1,\ldots,X_e,T_1,\ldots,T_s]]/(I)$ with the induced map the coefficient inclusion. Denote the maximal ideal of $R/I$ by $\mathfrak a$ and that of the second quotient by $\mathfrak b$. In particular these presentations preserve the actual map from $A$, not just the isomorphism classes of the two completions.

source.place: Coefficient-compatible refinement of Tag 07NQ, complete power-series presentation step.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-coefficient-extended-power-series-jets] to $R/I$ and $L[[X,T]]/(I)$ from step 2. Its map fixes the base coefficients, is multiplicative and preserves total degree. For $A$ and $B$, [lem-weil-pbc-local-completion-local-ring] identifies the completed maximal ideals with their extended maximal ideals. Part (2) of [lem-weil-pbc-module-completion-complete] identifies the quotients by every positive power with those before completion. These are the canonical ring quotient maps, so they preserve multiplication and the map from $A$ to $B$. Taking consecutive kernels (degree zero uses the quotient by the maximal ideal itself) identifies the associated graded rings. Compose with the cited graded isomorphism; its constant-$T$ part is the actual induced base map, as required.

source.place: Tag 05GG (lemma-hathat-finitely-generated), part (2), and Tag 05GI (lemma-radical-completion); finite-jet lemma and canonical kernel assembly.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-flat-local-component-dimension-difference] with $k=\mathbf Q$ to the flat local map in step 1: minimal primes contract surjectively, and each pair $(\mathfrak p,\mathfrak q)$ satisfies the stated dimension-difference formula. A minimal prime $\mathfrak q$ of $B=P_{\mathfrak N}$ corresponds to a minimal prime $\mathfrak Q\subseteq\mathfrak N$ of $P$: every smaller prime survives localization. Apply [lem-trf-smooth-chart-generic-residue-transcendence] to this pair. It gives $\operatorname{trdeg}_{\operatorname{Frac}(A/\mathfrak p)}\operatorname{Frac}(B/\mathfrak q)=r=s+\operatorname{trdeg}_K L$. Substitution yields $\dim(B/\mathfrak q)=\dim(A/\mathfrak p)+s$. Surjective contraction proves both inclusions of the required sets.

source.place: Assembly of the flat-local dimension-difference and smooth-chart generic-residue lemmas; the final set argument of former step 9.
